fatal_errors: Does not identify the specific AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy or its as-cast FCC+B2 state.
Misattributes the transition to generic resistance to temper embrittlement rather than enhanced L12 ordering and jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Predicts a ductile-brittle-ductile transition 'without a dramatic loss of ductility,' contradicting the defining brittle minimum observed after aging near 600°C.
Omits the approximately 550–750°C aging window, the 600°C ductility minimum, and recovery near 750°C.
Provides no evidence capable of distinguishing phase-boundary-mediated plastic instability from classical impurity-segregation temper embrittlement.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes only the broad topic—temperature-dependent ductility in compositionally complex alloys—and supplies a conventional-alloy comparison. It fails to reconstruct the material, aging treatments, microstructural mediators, mechanism, and non-monotonic result. Its proposed experiment measures only bulk ductility and cannot test the key prediction of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged B2/FCC boundary tips or exclude grain-boundary impurity segregation. With no cited evidence and an internally contradictory outcome, it is not a supported reconstruction.
